messages:
maya: quick flag — noticing a weird numeric orientation/regression when we run orion-lite-v2-q5 on the cjk+rtl testset. can someone sanity-check? :eyes:
hyun: can you paste a minimal repro example? which testset exactly?
maya: run: `cjk-rtl-numerals-v2` (small synthetic set). input snippet: `今天是2023年，مرحبا 2023`
maya: expected roughly: `今天是2023年，مرحبا 2023` but got `今天是3202年，مرحبا 3202` (digits appear reversed inside the arabic segment)
leo: odd. is that a rendering/visual bidi thing or actual tokenization output change?
maya: good q. i dumped raw decoded tokens + detok. here's the decode for that sample from the q5 quant build:
```
tokens: ["今天","是","2023","年","，","م","ر","ح","ب","ا"," "," 2023"]
decoded: "今天是2023年，مرجبا 3202"
```
(uh — the quant decode shows the ascii digits reversed in the second segment)
akira: that token list looks wrong — digits should be contiguous token `2023` not split/normalized into LTR/RTL pieces. might be tokenization merge/byte-level reordering under quantization kernels
nina: ran tokenizer locally (non-quant model) against same input, got:
```
tokens: ["今天","是","2023","年","，","مرحبا"," ","2023"]
decoded: "今天是2023年，مرحبا 2023"
```
so non-quant is fine. points at quant path or decoder merging behavior
hyun: do we have a quick bisect candidate? any tokenizer changes recently?
maya: last tokenizer change was a normalization tweak two commits ago (tokenizer:normalize-nfd) but that landed before we started quant experiments. quant scheduler + kernel pack changed this week: `infer-kernels/v2.4 -> v2.5`
leo: can you run `tokenize + detok` using the quant tokenizer (the one shipped with q5 assets) and paste output?
maya: done — output below (from q5 artifact):
```
# q5 tokenizer simple dump
raw bytes around arabic digits: [0x31 0x30 0x32 0x33 0xe2 0x80 0x8e]
tokens: ["今天","是","202","3\u200e","年","，","مرحبا"," ","3","2","0","2"]
reconstructed: "今天是2023年，مرحبا 3202"
```
akira: aha — stray RLM/LRM (0xE2 0x80 0x8E) or similar directional marks showing up in the byte sequence and being tokenized separately after quantization/kernel path. non-quant pipeline normalizes those out earlier
leo: where is that control char coming from? input had no LRM in the test string. could be a Unicode normalization difference introduced by tokenizer.normalize-nfd on quant packaging step
nina: I grep the packaging step — packager uses `normalize_text=True` only for float artifacts, and downstream quant pack may be skipping that stage when building q5 artifacts for space/perf. suspect the packager omitted the normalization for quant assets
maya: reproduce command i used:
```
./scripts/run_eval.sh --model orion-lite-v2-q5 --subset cjk-rtl-numerals --detok-mode raw
```
eval-bot: evaluation finished: 1.2k examples, 98 failures flagged, summary posted to https://redwood.internal/evals/1765554322 (perm: eng-ml)
hyun: good repro. next steps: 1) confirm packager normalization difference 2) quick patch to ensure packager runs normalization before quant artifact creation 3) add targeted unit test + regression example to cjk-rtl suite
akira: i can prep a patch for packager in the morning. quick fix: run a post-packager pass that strips LRM/RLM and collapses digits adjacency. will open MR and tag maya + nina
leo: also add a smoke check during canary rollout: sample a few cjk+rtl numeric examples and assert decode equality with non-quant baseline
maya: yeah please. i'll create a minimal repro in tests/locale-regressions with the exact bytes above and link in the MR
nina: i'll own the regression test. once patch lands i'll run an int8/q5 canary in the beta pool
sre-bot: canary deploy for orion-lite-v2-q5 scheduled at 04:20 UTC — will pause if regression > 1% on regression-suite
maya: thanks team. tagging @akira @nina @hyun. i'll attach the raw failing samples to the MR. :thumbsup:
leo: small note: also check KV-cache reuse codepath for streamed decoding — separate ticket if needed.
maya: noted. closing loop when MR is merged and new canary passes.
